text:
Bathroom shooting
The guy shot a guy in the shower in the chest. 
He shot at the guy in the shower first, my father say where the bullet hit, turned to help the guy injured, the guy with the gun then pointed the gun at my father and aimed it at him

Sargent Weaver showed up. He was an E5.

The guy with the gun was drunk with eyes rolled to the back of his head. He passed out.

Airforce police showed up. Took my father’s statement. The guy was from a different company / unit.

Happened at Tah San hut headquarters company, right next to his hooch. 

Father didn’t know the guy showering.

Heard the shooter knew the guy in the shower, and he was imprisoned in Okinawa of hard labor for 20 years.
researchNotes: Larry's words relayed third-person by his son, who typed on his own @mdfmkl account during the 2026-08-15 session (Larry dictating at the table). The fullest account yet of the bathroom shooting (unresolved #11; timeline entry data/timeline/1965-02-bathroom-shooting.json). New findable details: the victim was shot in the chest (a wounding, so medical records exist); Air Force police took the statement (Air Force security-police blotters are a second record path besides the court-martial); the sentence Larry heard — 20 years hard labor, imprisoned in Okinawa — matches period confinement practice. Sgt. Weaver enters as the responding NCO. Earlier fragments (2026-08-13 comment, and the family knife memory in 2026-brief-bathroom-knife.json) are preserved; discrepancies stand.
